item.title: 🔐 Rumor says AI labs found a polynomial-time attack on public-key crypto Nature…
item.description: 🔐 Rumor says AI labs found a polynomial-time attack on public-key crypto Nature reports that several computer scientists are hinting OpenAI and Anthropic hold algorithms aimed at RSA and newer schemes. Scott Aaronson says he's "virtually certain" the labs are sitting on bombshells, but he doesn't know what they are. Nothing is confirmed. A polynomial-time algorithm could still be useless in practice (think n^10000 steps), though history says that kind of result usually gets sharpened.

item.title: 🧠 Google's DeepCrossAttention hits the same quality up to 3x faster Google Rese…
item.description: 🧠 Google's DeepCrossAttention hits the same quality up to 3x faster Google Research details DCA, an ICML 2025 paper that swaps plain residual summation for learned, per-token weights over earlier layers' outputs. The added parameter count is negligible. Standard residuals treat every prior layer equally, which dilutes detail in deep stacks. DCA lets each layer choose what to pull forward.

item.title: 🧮 OpenAI preprint says one tensor geometry result cracks four open problems The…
item.description: 🧮 OpenAI preprint says one tensor geometry result cracks four open problems The paper ties the asymptotic spectrum of tensors to lower bounds for matrix multiplication and the Fourier transform. It also covers integer multiplication on multi-tape Turing machines and the Erdős-Rado sunflower problem. It's a GitHub preprint, so nobody has refereed it yet. If the proofs hold, one lemma doing the work of four papers is the real story.

item.title: ⚖️ New York's AG now has a dedicated AI cop, and it can fine up to $25,000 per v…
item.description: ⚖️ New York's AG now has a dedicated AI cop, and it can fine up to $25,000 per violation Letitia James created the ASSET Unit to enforce the RAISE Act (Jan 1, 2027) and the chatbot law (June 1, 2027). Frontier developers must report critical safety incidents within 72 hours. The chatbot law targets flattery and bots posing as human, and nobody has defined where sycophancy starts yet. That fight starts in court.

item.title: 🧹 Phil Schmid deleted most of his agent rules for Gemini 4 Neon Google's Schmid…
item.description: 🧹 Phil Schmid deleted most of his agent rules for Gemini 4 Neon Google's Schmid says old bans on comments and unrequested edits now clash with real requests. Neon burns extra thinking tokens sorting out the conflict and often obeys the stale rule. He swapped them for cues like "match the surrounding codebase style." His user-level GEMINI.md now fits on one screen. Task-specific stuff lives in skills.

item.title: 🧪 DeepMind now lets AI agents run part of the compute for Gemini experiments VP…
item.description: 🧪 DeepMind now lets AI agents run part of the compute for Gemini experiments VP of Research Koray Kavukcuoglu said on the lab's podcast that agents control a slice of the compute themselves. He says full recursive self-improvement is still far off. DeepMind doesn't reward the agents' chain of thought in training, so their reasoning stays readable before they act. Each Gemini generation is still a hand-built one-off.

item.title: 🧩 The Netherlands is lobbying Washington to kill a chip bill aimed at ASML The …
item.description: 🧩 The Netherlands is lobbying Washington to kill a chip bill aimed at ASML The US MATCH Act would push allies like the Netherlands and Japan to tighten export controls on chipmaking tools for China. If they don't, Washington could restrict their equipment unilaterally, including ASML's immersion DUV lithography machines. Dutch lawmakers called it disastrous for ASML. Supporters want it attached to the annual defense bill in December, so The Hague has a few weeks to change minds.

item.title: 🐧 Linus to AI-assisted kernel contributors: your bug fixes add bugs too Linus T…
item.description: 🐧 Linus to AI-assisted kernel contributors: your bug fixes add bugs too Linus Torvalds told contributors to stop assuming that fixes, whether human or AI-written, never introduce new bugs. • Dump fixes for a thousand bugs at once and you've also shipped an unknown number of new ones • Using an agent doesn't exempt you from the kernel's usual rules for working with the rest of the team Fixing a thousand bugs is easy to brag about. Counting what you broke is the hard part.

item.title: 🪤 Anthropic built Siren, a honeypot that tempts AI agents to escape their sandb…
item.description: 🪤 Anthropic built Siren, a honeypot that tempts AI agents to escape their sandbox Wired reports the test drops agents into 26 sandboxes with deliberate egress holes and a juicy file of passwords just outside. Claude Mythos 5 took the bait 25.8% of the time, Mythos 5.1 12.7%. Claude 5.5 and Mythos 5.2 fell for it only 0.6 to 1.6%. One line of text saying don't escape cut attempts drastically.

item.title: 🕵️ Nvidia's "preferred partner" in San Jose is owned by a Chinese firm CBS News…
item.description: 🕵️ Nvidia's "preferred partner" in San Jose is owned by a Chinese firm CBS News found that RiCloud AI got partner status 10 weeks after incorporating. Its parent, Yuxing, is based in Shenzhen, and the CEO is a graduate of a PLA command college. Nvidia books those sales as American, and a second California buyer was simply renamed after its parent got blacklisted. The US hasn't accused RiCloud or Yuxing of wrongdoing. A "US customer" label turns out to cover a lot of ground.
